image_description: A close-up, top-down view of a marine mollusk identified as a chiton. The organism has an elongated, oval shape with a distinct dorsal surface featuring eight overlapping, textured calcareous plates (valves) arranged in a linear series. These plates are embedded in a thick, leathery girdle covered in dense, bristle-like spines. The coloration is mottled with shades of grey, brown, and tan, blending with the rocky substrate it appears to be clinging to. No head, eyes, or tentacles are visible, consistent with the reduced head structure of chitons.
